approachQuestion.prompt: A workshop receives one load value per shift. For each shift i, return the length of the longest contiguous suffix ending at i in which every load is at most load[i]. Include shift i itself. Loads may repeat and may be negative. Example: [8, 3, 3, 6, 9] returns [1, 1, 2, 3, 5]. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Scan left to right with a stack of (load, span) pairs. Start span at 1; pop all top loads at most the current load and add their spans. Emit the span and push the current pair.
options.feedback: Each popped block is contiguous immediately before the accumulated suffix and contains no value larger than the current load. The first remaining larger load is exactly the stopping boundary.

options.text: Keep indices in strictly decreasing load order. Pop loads at most the current load; emit i minus the top index, or i+1 if empty, then push i.
options.feedback: The remaining top is the nearest earlier strictly larger load. Its distance gives the same suffix length without storing block sizes.

options.text: Use load/span blocks, but pop only loads strictly smaller than the current load.
options.feedback: Equal loads belong to the suffix too. For [3, 3], this emits [1, 1] instead of [1, 2].

options.text: For each shift, walk backward until a strictly larger load or the array start is reached.
options.feedback: This computes the requested spans, but an increasing sequence repeats nearly the entire prefix search for each shift, making it clearly inefficient at the input limit.

feedback.reason: Compress dominated earlier positions into blocks while preserving their total span.
details: For each load begin a new span of one. Merge top blocks whose load is at most this load, summing their spans, then emit and push the combined block. A larger top stays as the stopping boundary.

Merged blocks summarize consecutive earlier loads no greater than the current load. Sum their spans rather than their values. A remaining strictly greater top stops the span, so equal loads must merge too.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For merge-load-blocks, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of shifts. Emit each answer into a separately allocated result array; no prefix is copied.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each span block is inserted once and merged away at most once.
details: A merged span block is popped only once, then represented by the newly pushed aggregate. Summing span values is constant-time word arithmetic; it does not revisit the block's original shifts. Hence total work is O(n), while strictly decreasing loads retain n separate blocks. Sorting would lose arrival-order span semantics.
